releases.name: AbyssME 0.8.0 Beta 1
releases.body:
AbyssME now brings 24 platforms together on ARM64. The new platform gallery lets you pick a device and browse its games. Turn on **Show platforms without games** to find a new system, install its firmware if needed, and add your first game.

Alongside Java ME, Mophun, Symbian and N-Gage, the ARM64 edition includes WIPI / SKVM, Dingoo A320, Gemei A330, Aquaplus P/ECE, Watara Supervision, Mega Duck, Cybiko, Flash Lite, Gamate, Palm OS, Palm webOS, Firefox OS, KaiOS, Atari Portfolio, early iPhone OS, Arduboy / FX, Gamebuino Classic, Pokitto, original Thumby and ESPboy. The ARMv7 edition includes Java ME and Mophun.

**Download** the standard APK for ARM64 or the APK marked **armv7** for a 32-bit ARM device. Both require Android 10 or later. Install over the previous official APK to keep your games and saves. Supply your own games and system files.

[Setup guide](https://abysstail.art/guides/abyssme-setup.html) · [Source and build instructions](https://github.com/EriArk/JavaEmulator/blob/v0.8.0-beta.1/docs/releases/v0.8.0-beta.1.md)

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 10
releases.body:
# AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 10

Beta 10 adds **global physical-controller profiles** and improves Mophun sound and game speed.

Open **Settings → Physical controller profiles** to edit the global mapping or create reusable profiles for buttons and both sticks. Assign them to games from the manager or each game's Controls page. Graphics, touch layouts and physical mappings stay independent. Existing per-game overrides take priority; shared changes apply the next time the game opens. Profiles are included in library backups.

Mophun sound is now enabled for every game. Short BEEP effects and `vBeep` are supported, and PCM follows pause and emulation speed. A common phone-model execution budget reduces excessive speed in CPU-dependent games such as the supplied Boulder Dash and Lemtris versions.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.10.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and experimental Symbian/N-Gage.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.10-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Android 10+ is required. Both update the existing app in place. Back up important saves before updating or switching architecture. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 9
releases.body:
Beta 9 adds **independent right-stick mapping** for physical controllers.

Open **Controls → Controller mapping → Sticks** to assign the right stick’s directions and diagonals to phone keys, soft keys or Fire. **Identify** detects right-stick movement; pressing R3 remains a separate input. Bindings are saved per game, and existing profiles keep their settings with the new directions unbound.

The shared input path supports Java ME, Mophun and Symbian/N-Gage. This maps stick directions to digital keys; it does not add proportional analog camera support to games.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.9.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and experimental Symbian/N-Gage.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.9-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Android 10+ is required. Both update the existing app in place.

Tested with automated input and a virtual joystick on Retroid; physical dual-stick hardware testing remains pending. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 8
releases.body:
Beta 8 fixes Lara's black/striped appearance and loading-screen text showing through her model in **Tomb Raider: Underworld 3D**. The cause was incorrect transparency when transferring M3G rendering to the Java ME screen.

Startup errors now show the original game exception instead of only `InvocationTargetException`.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.8.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and the combined Symbian runtime.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.8-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Both require Android 10+ and update the existing app without uninstalling.

The reported **Crash Titans 1.3.7 Sony S700i JAR** was also checked. Its code and packed resources are inconsistent; the same reader fails on ordinary Java outside AbyssME. This release does not make that particular JAR playable.

Checks: 427 JVM tests per build, focused Retroid renderer tests, signed APK update and first-room checks. This is not complete-game acceptance. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 7
releases.body:
# AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 7

## Separate graphics and control profiles

- **Settings → Graphics profiles** and **Settings → Control profiles** now have
  independent global defaults, named profiles and assignments. Each game can
  select one graphics profile and one control profile. Changing or resetting
  one category leaves the other intact; extra Gamepad buttons remain available.
- Graphics profiles include supported scaling, smoothing, built-in xBRZ/CRT,
  FSR/sharpness, interpolation, LCD filters and capture settings. Java GPU and
  Mophun support GPU effects; Symbian uses its supported host display options.
  Integer scaling falls back to Fit on Symbian. Java-only geometry options are
  identified in the editor's support information.
- Beta 6 combined profiles split automatically: LCD inheritance and exceptions
  move to graphics, while touch settings remain in controls. Other existing
  graphics remain explicit overrides. Reset the relevant category's overrides
  when you want existing games to inherit a shared setup.
- Both catalogs, including unassigned profiles, travel through library backups.
  Phone backups retain portable game definitions. Picture Keep/Undo preserves

releases.name: v1.2.0
releases.body:
It is my pleasure to announce a new version of Hades!

There's a ton of new and exciting features on this one, I'm happy it's finally landing in your hands 😁. 

Among others, this release provides:

## **Highlights**:
- **Cheat code support**:  with all three major cheat devices: GameShark, CodeBreaker and Pro Action Replay v3 (PARv3)
- **xBRZ scaling filter**, for sharp, smooth visuals at high resolutions
- **Idle loop elimination**, to boost the performances of some of your favorite games

## **Emulation**:
- **ROM Mirroring support**, which fixes a bunch of input issues in the Classic NES Series games
- **OBJ rendering cycle limits**: sprites now have a per-scanline rendering budget, like the real PPU
- **PSG channels 2 and 3** are now resampled correctly each time their frequency changes
- **New color correction profiles** based on the work of Pokefan531 and Hunterk

## **Performance**:
- The scheduler now uses a **min-heap** to find the next event faster, giving a significant performance boost
- **Link-time optimizations (LTO)** are now enabled by default for release builds
- Fixed a performance issue when a file dialog was open

## Persona 5 Royal Android Recomp v0.5.12

### Español
- **Ocultar controles en pantalla:** Se añadió la opción en el Launcher (`NX_TOUCH_HIDE`) para ocultar los controles visuales. Los controles siguen 100% activos y funcionales al tocar la pantalla, ideal para quienes prefieren la pantalla limpia o juegan con memoria muscular.
- **Corrección de cierre inmediato al iniciar (Play crash):** Se protegió el acceso a JNI y verificación de permisos de almacenamiento en `android_main` para dispositivos cargando directo por NSP/FD (POCO X7 Pro, POCO F6, etc.).

- **Corrección de texto en mensajes (IM / SNS Chat):** Se corrigió el renderizado del texto en las opciones de respuesta del chat del teléfono móvil (PR #251).

releases.name: Need for Speed: Underground - Android v1.0.7
releases.body:
- Lower CPU load during races. Vulkan reuses uploaded vertex data, shader parameters, and descriptor sets. Index data is written directly into the rendering buffer, eliminating an intermediate copy.
- Fewer draw calls. Objects with matching geometry and compatible rendering state can now be drawn together in the main pass and in reflections. Each object keeps its own position and rendering parameters.
- Faster P8 texture handling. Paletted textures now use NEON decoding, and a texture cache fix reduces redundant decoding of textures that haven’t changed.
- Lower runtime overhead. Xbox thread scheduling checks, graphics command processing, and frequently used port routines take less CPU time.
- Lower audio processing overhead. The low-pass filter processes both channels in parallel, and diagnostic calculations run less often.
- Improved 30/60 FPS switching. The selected mode is applied through D3D frame presentation while preserving simulation speed and game timers.

releases.name: Copperline 1.2.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.2.0 is the second feature release of the 1.x series. It adds a video slot with an emulated NewTek Video Toaster 4000 and Video Flyer, an Amiga 2000 profile, a terminal display that also works over SSH, single-file web pages for floppy titles, high-density floppies and MP4 recording. The CPU core gains a long list of conformance fixes, and Copper, sprite, beam-counter and interrupt timing are corrected. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.1.0.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.2.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.

releases.name: Copperline 1.1.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.1.0 is the first feature release of the 1.x series. Hard drives can now run at the speed of the period drives each Amiga shipped with. The MMU-less 68EC030, 68EC040 and 68EC060 are new CPU choices. The JIT is much faster on fast-RAM code and heavy disk I/O, and has a new "fastest" speed. A500 CIA, interrupt and bus timing are corrected against measurements of a real A500. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.0.1.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.1.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.
- **Desktop save states from 1.0.x still load.** The CIA chunks are migrated to their new layout. A resumed 1.0.x state continues under the corrected timing, so it can drift from what 1.0.x would have produced (a factory A500 state from 1.0.1 still renders byte-identical frames). States saved by 1.1.0 do not load in 1.0.x, which reports that the state comes from a newer Copperline.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.1
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.1 is the first maintenance release for 1.0. Most of it fixes problems reported against 1.0.0: an AGA display fetch error, a blitter race on fast CPUs, warm reboots on the A3000 and A4000, the 68060 FPU at reset, the copperhf hard-disk driver, and a window-resize hang on Windows. Menu settings are now remembered between launches, and screenshots save the picture as you see it.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.1.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files still load: the save-state format has not changed, and a 1.0.0 state resumes byte-for-byte as it does in 1.0.0.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.0 is the first stable release. It follows two weeks of testing of 1.0.0-rc.1 and is the 23rd release since the source went public on 14 June.

This release adds Smart framing and native 1:1 screenshots, more control over where and how the window opens, VHD hard-disk images, a fix for AGA sprites that use scan-doubling, and a Check for updates button that only contacts GitHub when you press it.

## Copperline 1.0 at a glance

- **Machines:** A1000, A500, A500+, A600, A1200, A3000, A4000, CDTV and CD32, with OCS, ECS and AGA chipsets and 68000 to 68060 CPUs, FPUs and MMUs.
- **Accuracy:** the CPU and custom chips run on one colour-clock timeline, with the chip bus shared out cycle by cycle. Timing is checked against a real A1200, A4000 and CD32, and 45 test programs are compared pixel for pixel on every change.
- **Ready to run:** the open AROS ROM is bundled, as are ROMs for the A2091, A4091 and IDE boards, the CD32 FMV module and the HRTMon freezer. WHDLoad packages and Amiga programs boot directly.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0-rc.1: the first release candidate for 1.0
releases.body:
This is the first release candidate for Copperline 1.0. If testing does not turn up problems that need a second candidate, the next release will be 1.0.0.

This cycle brings three- and four-player netplay on the desktop, debugger watchpoints on device registers with a timed trace of CD32 drive commands, a refreshed AROS ROM, and a review of the whole manual against the program, which also found and fixed a few mismatches in the program itself.

Please try your usual games, demos and configurations with it. Anything that worked in 0.21.0 and does not work here is exactly what a release candidate is for: [open an issue](https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/issues) with the configuration and the software involved.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.0-rc.1.** The wire protocol moved to version 3 to carry up to four players, so a 0.21.0 peer cannot join.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files from 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 still load; states from 0.19 and earlier do not.

## O que mudou nesta branch (`fix/first-launch-crash`)

### Corrigido o crash na 1ª inicialização (selecionar ROM + Start Game fechava o app)
Na primeira execução do app, depois de selecionar a ROM e tocar em **Start Game**, o app fechava sozinho; na segunda inicialização funcionava perfeitamente. Causa raiz multi-fator, todas eliminadas:

- **Ciclo do seletor de ROM quebrava a sessão gráfica**: ao abrir o seletor (DocumentsUI), a surface Vulkan era destruída/recriada e a fila de present ficava congelada — o **Start Game** na MESMA sessão rodava em estado frágil (por isso o processo limpo da 2ª execução funcionava). # 0.60.1 is out

There was a bug in the AppImage Updater Code. To fix this i have to revert to the old AppImage build and wait several weeks to ensure a smooth update process.

# 0.60.0 is out 🎉

This release is special for me. I build emuze with web technologies because that’s where I have the most experience, and I’m really proud of what I’ve achieved over the years. I’ve always wanted to help out in this wonderful emulation community, but aside from testing, I couldn’t do much to help with the emulators I love because I struggled with C++ code, which most emulators are written in. But sometimes you feel forced to try and try again. Since v0.59.0, I’ve successfully added a [change to RMG](https://github.com/Rosalie241/RMG/pull/518) to use the SDL GUID to identify a gamepad more reliably, and I forked Mednafen with [mednafen-sdl3](https://github.com/bmsuseluda/mednafen-sdl3) to greatly expand gamepad support. Those changes are just baby steps in the grand scheme of things, but they felt great, and I hope I can build on them in the future.

# 0.59.2 is out 🎉

This release is mostly preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0.
Besides this fuse2 is not necessary anymore and Metainfos for AppImage Managers e.g. AM are included.

Please let me know what you think of it in the [emuze discord](https://discord.gg/tCzK7kc6Y4).

## 💥 Features
- added AppImage Metainfos
- AppImage works without fuse2
- Preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0

# 0.59.0 is out 🎉

As you might now i love the simplicity of console gaming. You start the game and it just works. With emulation more often then not you have to provide more then just the game. You need things like a BIOS file, firmware or key files. I wanted to assist with this for a long time. With this release you can choose a folder where you can put your BIOS files and emuze will pick them up and configure the Emulators. Of course emuze will tell you if a required file is missing. On top of this emuze comes bundled with open source BIOS implementations for PlayStation, Game Boy Advance and NEO GEO. Of course you can use official BIOS files instead if you need by putting them in the BIOS folder. Sadly i was not able to achieve the same result for more complicated systems like PlayStation 3, WiiU and Switch. These systems require a installation of a firmware. I will try to tackle these in a future release.

Besides this i bundled and pre configured ScummVM and DOSBox Pure Unleashed.
Therefore the day is finally here: All 35 supported systems are pre configured and bundled now 🥳

# 0.58.0 is out 🎉

As one of the few nerdy kids in a small sleepy town in a country where arcade gaming was classified as gambling i could see lightgun games in magazines only. I had an NES and Captain N with his Zapper was sooo awesome to me. But when the time came that i could buy one with my own money the rise of flat panels began and with it the death of CRT TVs and Lightguns altogether. It was just a thing of the past, sadly.
But surprisingly the genre came back with the Wii and PS3 and there Pointer devices. Some years later camera based Lightguns came to the market and finally Lightgun gaming with the same and even higher precision is possible on flat panels.

releases.name: v0.5.12-alpha
releases.body:
## English

**Status:** Playable menus, paddock/garage, and on-track driving on ARM64 Vulkan (`-O3 + ThinLTO`); fixes blown-out bloom / pitch-black 3D scenes caused by `exp_adjust` texture fetch exponent bias and eliminates MSAA resolve log spam.

### Changes
- **SPIR-V texture `exp_adjust` fix (`spirv_translator_fetch.cpp`):** Extract the 6-bit signed `exp_adjust` (bits 13:18) from fetch constant **word 3** instead of **word 4** (which holds `LOD bias` and erroneously scaled non-zero-LOD-bias textures by `2^±bias`, causing extreme bloom blowout and black scenes on track).
- **Automatic shader/pipeline cache invalidation:** Bumped `SpirvShaderTranslator::Modification::kVersion` (`12` → `13`) so existing `.vk.xpso` caches rebuild automatically on update.
- **Resolve log spam fix (`draw.cpp`):** Downgraded `Incorrect resolve sample selected` from `REXGPU_WARN` to `REXGPU_DEBUG` when `gpu_cap_msaa` caps main-scene MSAA to 1x, eliminating per-frame I/O overhead.

---

## Русский

- **Persistent Vulkan shader & pipeline cache on Android:** Added `Seek(0, SEEK_SET)` after `OpenFile(..., "a+b")` in `pipeline_cache.cpp` (fixes Android bionic EOF positioning so cached pipelines reload on startup).

# IZPSX emulator 0.5.3

IZPSX runs PlayStation games on Nintendo Switch 2 through [IZ2S](https://github.com/byizmysh/IZ2S-Platform).

## Install

### Through IZ2S App library

1. Download [`izpsx-emulator-0.5.3.iza`](https://github.com/byizmysh/IZPSX-emulator/releases/download/v0.5.3/izpsx-emulator-0.5.3.iza).
2. In IZ2S, open **App library**, import the `.iza` file, and install it to the Switch 2 SD card. IZ2S installs the emulator in `SD:/iz2s/modules/izpsx/`. The installer includes the launcher, engine, shaders, font, and interface assets.

### Directly to the SD card

1. Download [`izpsx-emulator-0.5.3.zip`](https://github.com/byizmysh/IZPSX-emulator/releases/download/v0.5.3/izpsx-emulator-0.5.3.zip).
2. Extract the ZIP to the root of the Switch 2 SD card so `iz2s/` sits at the top level. The archive includes the emulator files and empty `bios/`, `games/`, and `saves/` folders under `SD:/iz2s/modules/izpsx/`.

Preserve your BIOS, games, memory cards, and settings when updating.

## BIOS and games

| File | SD card path |
| --- | --- |
| Your own PlayStation BIOS, exactly **512 KiB (524,288 bytes)** | `SD:/iz2s/modules/izpsx/bios/bios.bin` |

releases.name: v1.2.6: save backups, movies keep their shape, every controller works
releases.body:
**Save backups, movies that keep their shape, and two controllers at once.**

- **Save backups** (*CTRL → Game → Save backups …*): copies of all your save slots in a folder you choose, outside the app, so uninstalling the game doesn't delete them. A copy is made after the game saves, at most every 10 minutes. The latest 10 and one for each of the last 7 days played are kept, up to 64 MB in all (the latest 3 always). A backup can be restored from the same screen; it takes effect at the next start, and the saves it replaces are kept aside.
- **Movies are never stretched.** They keep their 16:9 shape with **Wide screen** on, and now also with **Stretch to fill wide screens** on. A movie whose own picture has black bars at the top and bottom as well (bars on all four sides) is zoomed in, centred, until one pair of bars is gone, without cutting anything off.
- **Controllers:** every connected controller now controls the game. Before, with two connected (for example a handheld's built-in controls and an external pad), the second one's buttons were ignored.

releases.name: v1.2.5: render resolution and true wide screens
releases.body:
**Choose the render resolution, and true wide screens.**

- **Resolution** (*CTRL → Image*, applies at the next start): **540p**, **720p** (as on the Xbox 360, the default) or **1080p**. The 3D world is drawn at that size; menus and the HUD stay sharp at 720p. 540p is faster and a little softer. 1080p is scaled down into the 720p picture, which smooths edges rather than adding detail, and needs a fast GPU.
- **Wide screen** (*CTRL → Image*, applies at the next start): on screens wider than 16:9 (most phones), the 3D world fills the whole screen, with more to see at the sides instead of black bars or stretching. Menus, the HUD and the minimap stay in the middle, laid out as on a 16:9 screen, and movies keep 16:9 with black bars. It costs some speed: on a Galaxy S10 (Adreno 640) the field runs at about 24.5 fps instead of 28. Off by default.
- With both left at their defaults, the picture is the same as in v1.2.4.

releases.name: v1.2.4: tidier CTRL menu with Exit game, fixes for more phones
releases.body:
**A tidier CTRL menu with Exit game, and fixes for more phones from the Dark Souls II port.**

- **CTRL menu:** the options are now in sections that open one at a time: *Controls*, *Frame rate and performance*, *Image*, *Second screen*, *Game* and *Troubleshooting*. **Exit game** (top right) closes the game after asking; save in the game's main menu first. After changing an option marked *, the menu offers to restart the game so it takes effect.
- **CTRL button:** under *Controls* it can stay on screen, slide into a small tab when not in use, or go away 30 seconds after the game starts. Once it's gone, Android's Back button or gesture opens the menu.
- **Frame rate:** one list with 30, 40, 60 and *60 fps, smoother* (the former 120 Hz option).
- **Mali GPUs (Dimensity, Exynos, Tensor):** the app now starts on Arm's own driver, with the renderer settings that fixed Mali players' glitches in the Dark Souls II port, which shares this renderer. Still untested on a real Mali phone: reports with logs are welcome.
- **Adreno 8xx (Snapdragon 8 Elite):** Turnip now runs in sysmem mode there, which fixed GPU hangs on these chips in the Dark Souls II port.

releases.name: v1.2.3: fix for Adreno 600-series GPUs
releases.body:
**Fix for Adreno 600-series GPUs (Snapdragon 855 / 865 / 870 / 888 and similar).**

- **Adreno 6xx:** the renderer no longer loses work on these GPUs. Missing menu text, garbled or black pictures and wrong colours came from the Turnip driver on Adreno 6xx dropping some of the renderer's compute work (texture loads and render-to-texture copies) when it was set up while a drawing pass was still open. The fix closes the pass first. It was found by the Dark Souls II port's frame capture on an Adreno 640 and tested here on a Galaxy S10 (Adreno 640) (#4). Adreno 7xx/8xx draw the same as before, at the same speed.

**Updating from v1.2.2:** install `lr-recomp-android-arm64.apk` (below) over it. Your saves, game files, shaders and settings are kept.

releases.name: v1.2.2: infinite HP, stretch to fill wide screens
releases.body:
**Infinite HP, and a stretch option for wide phone screens.**

- **Infinite HP (in battle):** a new cheat under **CTRL → Cheats**. Lightning's HP goes back to its maximum after every hit. A single hit larger than her maximum HP can still knock her out (#5).
- **Infinite EP** checked in battle, including the first tutorial battle: Overclock and the other EP abilities are refilled at once (#5).
- **Stretch to fill wide screens:** a new option under **CTRL → Image**. On phones wider than 16:9 it removes the black bars at the sides by stretching the picture sideways. It applies the next time the game starts (#6).
- **Regression tests:** a battle test for both cheats on the Thor.

**Updating from v1.2.1:** install `lr-recomp-android-arm64.apk` (below) over it. Your saves, game files, shaders and settings are kept.

releases.body:
Translation mods for Awakening and the DLC.

### Mods

- **Translations of Awakening and every DLC** (issue #7). A translation's talk tables
  (.tlk) for Awakening and the DLC replace the game's own of the same name, as the main
  game's do.
  - Put them in a mod like any other files, then choose **Convert for this version** if they
    were made for the PC.
  - Tested with a Korean translation in the main campaign, Awakening, Leliana's Song, The
    Darkspawn Chronicles, The Golems of Amgarrak and Witch Hunt, and in the DLC played from
    the main campaign.
  - A language whose letters the game's font does not have (Korean, for example) also needs
    a font made for the Xbox 360 version. Without one, its text shows as boxes.

  game's own id, for example `DAO_PRC_EP_1` for Awakening.
  - **Convert for this version** now puts its files in the mod's override folder, where they
    replace the add-in's own.
  - Before, it was installed as a second add-in, and the game did not use its files.
  - If you converted such a mod with an earlier version, delete it in **Mods** and add it
    again.

- **An external controller can play** (issue #6). Pressing Start on it used to bring up a
  profile sign-in that never finished, because the game only took the handheld's own
  controller as player 1.
  - Now the controller you use is player 1: press a button on it, or push a stick or trigger
    firmly, and it takes over. The handheld's own controller takes it back the same way.
  - A controller connected while you play works too.
  - Tested on the AYN Thor with its own controller. If you play with an external one, please
    tell us in issue #6 how it goes.

- **From 0.2.0-alpha to 0.2.5-alpha:** the launcher installs this update under **Launch Dragon
  Age**. No Build again is needed. Your saves, game data and settings stay.
- **From 0.1.9-alpha or earlier:** the launcher installs it too, and then shows **Build again**.
  Choose it once (about eight minutes).

releases.name: WoW Mobile v0.1.2
releases.body:
Fixes the ConsolePort wizard reappearing on every login ([reported on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/EmulationOnAndroid/)).

If you interacted with the addon's controller-setup wizard during your very first login, WoW saved a half-finished configuration that blocked the automatic setup from ever applying — so the wizard kept coming back. The app now re-checks your account every time you press PLAY and repairs that state automatically (your previous file is kept as `ConsolePort.lua.bak`).

**If you were affected:** update, exit the game completely, press PLAY again. The wizard should be gone and the full pad mapped.

Also clarifies the first-login instructions shown in the app. Non-English clients (frFR, deDE, …) are fully supported — the locale was unrelated to this bug.

On first launch the app installs the bundled ConsolePortLK addons, calibrates the bindings, sets the realmlist (changeable in WoW Settings) and creates a tuned Wine container. After your first login, log out once so it can finish per-account calibration — then everything just works.

A stability and hygiene patch for v2.0.0, focused on the crash and antivirus reports from the first few hours.

## Downloads

- Windows: `Skate3Recomp-Windows.zip`
- Linux: `Skate3Recomp-Linux.zip`
- macOS: `Skate3Recomp-macOS.zip`

## Changes

#### Stability

- Fixed a crash on Linux and macOS where the game could die suddenly during gameplay when world streaming revoked memory the renderer was reading
- Fixed distant demoted tree trunks rendering with a flat blue texture

#### Antivirus false positives

- The Windows executable and runtime DLL now carry proper version metadata, and the runtime no longer contains any ability to create executable memory (it never used it - all game code is compiled at build time); both changes target the machine-learning heuristics some antivirus engines were tripping on
- A false-positive report has been filed with Microsoft for the v2.0.0 files; if your antivirus quarantined the runtime, restore it or re-download this release

#### Diagnostics

- The game now logs its exact build version at startup, so support logs identify the build they came from

The entire game renders natively at close visual parity with the console output, with a set of optional modern graphics enhancements that seek to go beyond it.

- Skills from items work on the buttons too, such as Teleport from Enigma or a staff, and charges.
- Teleport at once is now on by default: a tap jumps right away, holding keeps jumping, like Diablo II: Resurrected on a controller. Switched off (Settings › Controls › Skill buttons) you aim with the ring and jump when you let go, now without a pause.
- Joystick: it now stays where your thumb comes down. "Follows the thumb" is still there and no longer wanders off to the right; its dead zone can be set.

What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.

releases.name: v0.4.8
releases.body:
Co-op settings no longer have to match between friends, players 3 and up get their own Centaur in the tank chapter, and the native renderer stops smearing textures on AMD cards. Everything from [0.4.7](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.7) is included.

## Co-op

- **The host's settings apply to everyone in that campaign.** Before, a friend whose co-op settings differed from the host's (player count, extra players ending the game, and so on) did not see the campaign at all. Now only the release has to match: friends see the host's campaign whatever their own `gow2_coop_players` and co-op options say, and the host's settings decide how that campaign plays. Campaigns from a different release still stay hidden, and since 0.4.8 that check covers two-player games too.
- **One Centaur per player in the tank chapter.** When Marcus drives the Centaur, every player 3 and up gets a tank of their own next to him instead of hanging off his. If someone leaves their tank, dies, or falls too far behind, they get a new one next to Marcus; the extra tanks go away when the tank section ends. `gow2_coop_tanks = false` turns it off.

releases.name: v0.4.7
releases.body:
Phones get new defaults that run smoother and cooler, voices on Android should come through again, and every platform gets a Render scale option. Everything from [0.4.6](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.6) is included.

## Android

- **Frame rate unlocked with a 45 fps limit, by default.** Uncapped, the phone's GPU runs at full load until the phone lowers its clock as it heats up; the limit keeps headroom. The limit drops to the nearest rate that divides your screen's refresh, so every frame lasts the same: 40 fps on a 120 Hz screen (Galaxy S24/S25), 45 at 90 Hz, 30 at 60 Hz. On an S25 Ultra frame times went from a 25/25/16.7 ms mix to an even 25 ms. You can still pick 30, 60 or no limit in Device Options > Display > Frame rate limit.
- **Render scale 75 % by default.** The 3D scene is drawn at 75 % and scaled up to the screen; on an S25 Ultra that is 14 % less GPU work per frame, with a slightly softer picture. Graphics > Render scale goes back to 100 %.
- **Snapdragon GSR for the final upscale by default**, one pass instead of FSR 1's two.

releases.name: v0.4.6
releases.body:
Insane can now be picked from the start. Everything from [0.4.5](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.5) is included; if you have not read its notes, they cover the Riftworm fix for Vulkan, GPU detection on Linux and Proton, and the co-op go-to-player-1 key.

## Every platform

- **Insane without finishing the campaign first.** The option from 0.4.5, now named **All chapters and Insane unlocked** (PC Options > Saves, on by default), also enables the Insane button in the difficulty menu, in solo Campaign and in the co-op lobby. Before, the game greyed it out until the campaign had been finished once. As with chapters, only the menu check changes: your saved progress and the Extras list of unlockables are not touched.

## Known, still open

- Lighting that looks pixelated on Linux with presets above Low, and black textures on Low on Windows (both on a Legion Go): we could not reproduce them on our PC. A screenshot and the `logs/gow2_*.log` of the run, with the chapter, help a lot.

releases.name: v0.4.5
releases.body:
The Riftworm interior no longer crashes or goes black with Vulkan, the game picks the right GPU settings on Linux and under Proton, every chapter can be picked from the start, and co-op gets a key and a controller combo to go to player 1. Everything from [0.4.4](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.4) is included.

## Vulkan (Linux and SteamOS, Proton with Vulkan, Android, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Inside the Riftworm (act 5) no longer loses the GPU.** The worm's flesh is drawn with tessellation, and the shaders the renderer builds for it read their settings from the wrong slot, so the tessellation factor came from unrelated memory: the scene stayed black, would not load, or the game closed with a lost device. Fixed in SDK patch 0091 (found with the Khronos validation layer). On a Radeon RX 7800 XT the worm interior now runs 120 s at 60 fps where it failed within seconds. Under Proton, Vulkan (`gpu_backend = vulkan`) is the backend to use for that chapter: D3D12 through vkd3d-proton was also reported to lose the device there and we could not test it.

## Linux and SteamOS

releases.name: v0.4.4
releases.body:
Less memory traffic on phone GPUs, less work per draw on the GPU command thread, and a new option for the CPU core the game spins while it waits for the GPU. Everything from [0.4.3](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.3) is included.

## Vulkan (Android, Linux and SteamOS, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Each render pass now covers only what it draws.** The renderer sizes its render targets for the console's whole EDRAM (1520x3456 on the phone) and every render pass loaded and stored all of it, even when its draws touched only the 1280x720 of a 720p frame. Phone GPUs render in tiles and pay for every byte a pass loads and stores, so they moved about 5.7 times the memory they needed. Now each pass begins with only the area its draws and clears can write (SDK patch 0089). It follows the Vulkan rules, so the picture should not change; it has not been measured on a phone yet. If part of the picture looks missing or stale, set `vulkan_tight_render_area = false` in `gow2.toml` (it takes effect at once) and open an issue with the scene. Direct3D 12, the Windows default, is not affected.

## Every platform

releases.name: shadps4 v0.18.0 - codename UltraPersona
releases.body:
shadPS4 v0.18.0 "UltraPersona"

Hello there, it hasn't been a while, has it? While not much time has passed since our last stable release, we are here again with a brand new one. The main reason for this release is broken shadNet authorization in certain cases on the 0.17.0 release, but we have some more interesting new features as well.

Firstly, after some fixes, AvPlayer can now be loaded as LLE, meaning that you need the `libSceAvPlayer.sprx` (and `libSceAvPlayerStreaming.sprx`) module(s), which makes broken videos in a few games now work properly.

The above change was enabled by calling `sceLibcInternalMemoryMutexEnable` in LLE LibcInternal at boot, found by [@liuk7071](https://github.com/liuk7071), the developer of ChonkyStation4, another PS4 emulator.

A kernel event flag rewrite has also fixed Shadow of the Colossus often hanging on boot, and the game now consistently gets to menus.

releases.body:
# NSP Box 4.0.0 — Meet NUP

Smaller archives, flexible packaging, and more control over your game collection. Version 4.0 introduces **NUP Tools**, alongside the existing NSP builder.

### Package more. Store less.

- **Create compressed NUP archives** from extracted game folders, with base games, updates and DLC together in one file.
- **Choose your balance:** Fast for quicker compression, Balanced for everyday use, or Smaller for stronger compression. Incompressible files are stored raw automatically.
- **Keep what you need:** select Base, Updates and DLC independently. Choices appear after inspection, only for content present in your source. Latest-snapshot mode merges the newest selected update with the selected base, retains required base-only files, and leaves superseded versions behind. Turn it off to keep separate base/update records.
- **Avoid duplicate storage:** identical file contents can share the same space inside an archive.
- **Stay compatible:** leave files larger than 256 MiB uncompressed to reduce temporary decompression work in supported emulators.

### Convert, extract and check

- **NSP → NUP:** compress plaintext NSPs created by NSP Box.

releases.name: WinLite v1.4.0
releases.body:
# WinLite v1.4.0

## Overview
A release focused on rendering smoothness, a new X11 server and Steam support.

---

## 🎮 BETA - Steam
- Steam client support added.

---

## 🖥️ X11 server (rewritten in Rust)
The built-in X server has been rewritten from scratch in Rust and now covers much more of the X11 protocol.

**What you get**
- **Stability.** Memory-safe code removes a whole class of crashes and hangs.
- **Better game and launcher compatibility.** Newer screen-configuration (RANDR 1.2) and rendering extensions are supported, so Wine, launchers and games see a more complete environment.
- **Proper mouse cursors.** System cursors are drawn from a built-in cursor set, and colored/semi-transparent and animated cursors are supported.
- **Better frame pacing.** Frame presentation is synchronized with the real display refresh rate and with fences, which gives the renderer and the FPS limiter an accurate clock to work from.
- **Faster window drawing.** The shared frame buffer is locked once per operation instead of repeatedly, and more drawing requests (lines, rectangles, area clears) are handled directly.

Experimental, unofficial fork of xemu (original Xbox emulator) with a console-style dashboard, Xbox 360 games through your own Xenia, one-click 60 FPS patches, upscaling filters, CPU/GPU boost with per-game settings, and tools for finding out why a game is slow. Not supported by the xemu project.

Release body (paste into the GitHub release):
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Experimental, unofficial fork of xemu for trying out UI improvements. Not supported by the xemu project: please don't ask about it in xemu's Discord or GitHub.

Xbox 360 games, through your own Xenia. xemu does not emulate the Xbox 360, and this fork still doesn't include or change any 360 emulator. If you download Xenia or Xenia Canary yourself, the library can now list your 360 games and start them in it.

releases.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Experimental, unofficial fork of xemu for trying out UI improvements. Not supported by the xemu project: please don't ask about it in xemu's Discord or GitHub.
What's new in v2.4
Version in the title bar. The window now reads "xemu Modern GUI v2.4 | xemu v0.8.139", so it's easy to tell which build you're running.
Faster library scanning. Games appear as soon as they're found instead of after the whole folder has been read, several disc images are read at once, and extracted game folders (any folder containing `default.xbe`) are no longer searched file by file. Recycle-bin and hidden folders are skipped.

1.4 GHz CPU option. Real hardware speed can pace to 733 MHz (stock) or 1.4 GHz (like a modded console), under Settings > Performance. Real hardware speed is off by default.

releases.name: v2.3 – Faster games, NFL Fever 2004 fix, Linux build, Performance and compatibility release: CPU boost, GPU boost, per-game settings with automatic safe mode, a fix that lets NFL Fever 2004 run, and a first Linux build
releases.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Experimental, unofficial fork of xemu for trying out UI improvements. Not supported by the xemu project: please don't ask about it in xemu's Discord or GitHub.
What's new in v2.3
This release is about speed and game compatibility. The emulation changes are listed here so you know what touches the game itself.
CPU boost and GPU boost (Settings > General > Performance). CPU boost runs the game's SSE math on your PC's processor and trims work in the CPU emulation. GPU boost turns on faster paths in the graphics code, such as skipping textures a shader never reads. Turn either off if a game misbehaves. The ideas and some of the code come from Tovarichtch's xemu fork (branch `perf-experimental`).
Per-game settings and safe mode. Each game can have its own CPU boost, GPU boost and shader seeding, used the next time it starts (Settings > General > Performance > This game). If xemu closes unexpectedly while a boost was on, that game starts in safe mode the next time, with the boosts off, and tells you. "Leave safe mode" is in the same place.

## Changes

- **Less CPU time spent drawing each race frame.** The game's main thread now finds textures and sets them up for drawing with much less work, so busy frames with many objects on screen are less likely to run late, especially on phones that slow down when they get hot. - **The picture is unchanged on Windows:** the same Windows checks as 0.10.75 all passed (see below), and while PR #454 was tested, the new code drew the same 27 pictures bit for bit as 0.10.75 from the title screen up to the race (races themselves never repeat exactly, so they were compared by eye).

releases.name: Version 0.1.3

# Oblivion for Android 0.1.3

APK: `Oblivion-0.1.3.apk` (arm64-v8a, Android 9+, Vulkan 1.1).
SHA-1 `e74c55c378825480eedb6b2c781946bc4bef3555`

## Fixed
- Mali GPUs: geometry no longer explodes into streaks on Mali GPUs (Exynos, Dimensity, Tensor, Kirin), which lack the clip-distance feature.

## Performance
- Each thread keeps its own cache of recently freed small blocks and reuses them without taking the global heap lock. In testing, an allocate-and-free went from about 34 ms to 5 ms. Freeing the same block twice is still detected and logged though.
- A thread that re-enters a lock it already holds now just counts up the way Windows does, instead of going through the real lock each time.
- Memory copies: the base memcpy routine, about 10% of all CPU, now runs as Android's native copy.
- The game reads the clock hundreds of thousands of times a second. QueryPerformanceCounter, GetTickCount and timeGetTime now read the processor's hardware timer instead of making a system call.
- A missing Data folder is now remembered after the first check - no repeated path search and log line each time.

Please attach `port/log.txt` from your Oblivion folder to any bug report.

releases.name: MH Stories 2 port v0.1.0
releases.body:
## First public release

A native Android port of the console version of **Monster Hunter Stories 2: Wings of Ruin** for the **Retroid Pocket 5** and the **Retroid Pocket Flip 2**, running from your own copy of the game.

- **Early.** Tested on the Flip 2 with version 1.5.2 and its DLC: the title screen and a new game from the opening into Mahana Village. It has not been played much further, so later areas may still show problems.
- **A locked 30 fps.** The game asks for 60, but on the Flip 2 it reaches about 44–48 fps in the first village, so the port holds it at a steady 30. An empty file `60fps` in the game folder lifts the lock.
- **DLC.** The setup screen finds your DLC when each RomFS is in its own folder named with its title ID (as your extraction tool named it) or as `aoc/1`, `aoc/2`…
- **Setup screen.** The app asks for the folder with your extracted game files, checks them and starts the game. The ExeFS folder must be complete: besides `main` the game brings its own video library in `subsdk0`, and the app loads it. Prepared with 1.5.2; other versions are accepted with a notice.

releases.body:
天玑 / MediaTek X11 专版 · 合成器测试版

本版基于 1.2.0 天玑 X11 分支，**唯一改动是打开 KWin 合成器**，用于真机验证桌面特效（窗口晃动、魔灯等）能否真正生效。

#### 本版改了什么

此前每次启动桌面会话时，脚本都会把 `kwinrc` 强制改写为：

```ini
[Compositing]
Enabled=false
Backend=QPainter
```

这正是「在系统设置里勾了窗口晃动 / 魔灯，晃了半天毫无反应」的直接原因——**合成器关着，KWin 会静默忽略全部桌面特效**。

本版改为：

```ini
[Compositing]
Enabled=true
Backend=OpenGL
GLCore=false
LatencyPolicy=Low
WindowsBlockCompositing=false
```

后端固定为 **OpenGL（硬件）**，不使用纯软件 QPainter 后端；LLVM 软件渲染（llvmpipe / swrast）在部署时仍会被删除。

#### ⚠️ 这是未经验证的测试版，请只用于测试

发布者手上没有天玑真机，**本版没有在任何天玑设备上跑过**。请把预期放低。

已知的关键疑点（在我的机器上实测发现，属于**设备无关**的问题）：

1. **guest rootfs 内缺少 `virpipe_dri.so`**。逐个列出 rootfs 中全部 Mesa DRI 驱动后确认：有 `virtio_gpu_dri.so`、`zink_dri.so`、`panfrost_dri.so`、`mediatek_dri.so`，**但没有 `virpipe_dri.so`**——而这正是 VirGL 的 guest 端驱动。会话脚本仍在强制 `GALLIUM_DRIVER=virpipe` + `VTEST_SOCKET=/tmp/.virgl_test`，即**指向一个不存在的驱动**。若真机因此拿不到 GL 上下文，合成器就起不来。
2. **相反方向的证据**：发布者在高通测试机上开启 OpenGL 合成后桌面全黑，日志为 `MESA: error: ZINK: vkGetCalibratedTimestampsEXT failed (VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY)`。但那条日志同时说明 **KWin 当时确实拿到了 GL 上下文**（走的是 Zink）。这与第 1 点互相矛盾，怀疑 KWin 走 EGL 入口、Qt 走 GLX 入口，两者对 `GALLIUM_DRIVER` 的处理不同。
